A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CtrlRegen and CtrlRegen+. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. Algorithms moved from Section 3.3 to Appendix B can be matched directly.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark-removal experiments, image-quality measurements, noising-step sweeps and semantic/spatial control ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds inference-time measurements and a visual comparison at similar PSNR in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The semantic adapter, spatial control network, training objectives and inference procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 are relocated to Appendix B without procedural revisions; the mention of SD-v3 concerns future work.

E1.justification: Training datasets, evaluation datasets and the six watermark settings represented in results remain unchanged. Section 4.1 newly lists HiDDeN, but neither version reports identifiable HiDDeN results; v1 already claims seven evaluated methods while listing six. Whether this reflects additional tested coverage or a documentation correction is unresolved.

E2.justification: Regen and Rinse remain the main removal baselines. New Table 3 adds text-conditioned backbone Stable Diffusion as a timing comparator against CtrlRegen and CtrlRegen+. Figure 8 uses the existing Regen comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds a timing evaluation with CtrlRegen+ noising steps of 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1000. Its new StegaStamp comparison sets Regen to 360 steps to obtain PSNR comparable to CtrlRegen. These are additional protocols; the original benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 8 examines perceptual differences at similar PSNR using five StegaStamp examples. Table 3 analyzes computational cost across noising levels. The existing semantic/spatial ablation in Table 2 and noising-step analyses in Figures 5–7 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new timing results are reported as averages without run counts or uncertainty estimates, preserving the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. New Table 3 reports 1.74 seconds for backbone SD, 2.56 seconds for CtrlRegen and 0.69–2.64 seconds for CtrlRegen+ across tested noising levels. Figure 8 adds qualitative evidence of better content preservation at reportedly similar PSNR; it does not establish a revised same-setting benchmark score.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, attention equations and training objectives in Equations 1–5 remain unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs, and relocating the algorithms introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: Both retain the central claims of no-box watermark removal through controlled regeneration, effectiveness against high-perturbation watermarks and an adjustable removal/consistency trade-off. The shortened conclusion does not remove these claims from the paper or redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly acknowledges that regeneration consistency may be constrained by the backbone model. Appendix A interprets the timing overhead as small and extends the existing PSNR-versus-perceptual-quality discussion using the matched-PSNR examples. The original mechanism explanations remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address. Table 4 newly discloses payload lengths: 32 bits for DwtDctSvd, RivaGAN and SSL, 48 for StableSignature and 96 for StegaStamp. Table 3 adds inference costs. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original payload settings or implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds He et al. (2024) on LLM watermarking to the introduction and Esser et al. (2024) for the proposed future SD-v3 backbone. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to regeneration attacks, ControlNet and IP-Adapter remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 separates Section 4.2 into CtrlRegen and CtrlRegen+ subsections, condenses the conclusion, expands Appendix A and moves the algorithms to a new Appendix B. It also adds ethics and acknowledgement sections and makes limited wording and affiliation edits. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 8 and Tables 3–4, enlarges Table 2 and expands its caption, and reformats the relocated algorithms vertically. Figure 1 has revised axes and labels, including correction of 'Distantce'. The other existing visual evidence is retained, with limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility documentation through the code-access statement and payload lengths, adds useful runtime evidence, and supports its perceptual-quality argument with Figure 8. The backbone limitation also improves qualification of the claims. These gains are limited: the main experiments remain unchanged, and the new comparisons lack uncertainty estimates and numerical PSNR matching details.
